newsitem.title: USA: Mercury gets loan waiver extension.
newsitem.headline: Mercury gets loan waiver extension.

text.p: Troubled auto lender Mercury Finance Co. said Tuesday that it got an extension on a $50 million short-term loan it received a month ago from Bank of America.

The loan, used to meet operating expenses and make interest payments, was granted in February as Mercury tried to regroup from troubles that included overstated earnings, an FBI investigation and a slew of shareholder lawsuits.
The loan had been scheduled to come due on Monday unless Mercury got waivers it needed from other lenders.

Mercury said it was in talks with the lenders and that Bank of America had extended the deadline to March 14. It also said Bank of America has indicated it would extend the loan to June 10 if the waivers permit.

The waivers from the other lenders are needed since their loan agreements with Mercury restrict its ability to pledge assets as collateral. An auto lender such as Mercury needs a steady flow of available cash to do business.

On Jan. 29, Mercury said it would lower its earnings over the last four years by about $90 million due to accounting discrepancies it blamed on its controller, James Doyle. But a day later, Doyle's lawyer accused Mercury of a charade and said Doyle was cooperating with federal authorites.

Since then, Mercury has defaulted on millions of dollars in debt, been served with a search warrant by FBI agents seeking financial records, hired William Brandt Jr., a turnaround and bankruptcy specialist as chief executive officer, and has been named a defendant in more than half a dozen lawsuits over the misstated earnings.

The company's stock lost more than $2 billion in market value after the earnings cuts. The stock, which traded as high as $16 in the past year, rose 12.5 cents to $2.875 in early New York Stock Exchange trading.
